design_brief_poster.product: a concert poster for a jazz quartet
design_brief_poster.vibe: 1962 Blue Note sleeve energy, confident and spare

brief.concept_direction: Mid-century modern minimalism inspired by Reid Miles' Blue Note aesthetic, emphasizing high-contrast photography and structured negative space.
brief.composition: Asymmetrical layout using a strict grid system; place a high-contrast, grainy black-and-white photograph of the quartet occupying exactly 60% of the vertical space, aligned to the top-left, leaving the remaining 40% for bold, oversized typography.

typography.direction: Use a mix of heavy, condensed sans-serifs and elegant, thin-stroke serifs to create hierarchy.
typography.headline: Franklin Gothic Extra Condensed, set in all-caps, tracking tightened to -20, left-aligned.
typography.body: Baskerville or similar transitional serif, set at 10pt with generous leading, used only for essential concert details like venue, date, and time.

color_direction.direction: Duotone palette with a single dominant accent color.
color_direction.notes: Base the palette on a deep charcoal black (#1A1A1A) and a warm off-white paper texture (#F4F1EA), with one vibrant accent color (e.g., a saturated mustard yellow or cobalt blue) applied only to the headline or a single graphic element.

dos: Use a grainy, high-ISO film texture overlay on the entire image.
Align all text elements to a single vertical axis on the left side.
Limit the color palette to exactly three colors: black, off-white, and one accent color.
Use generous amounts of negative space to isolate the typography.
Ensure the photography is cropped tightly to emphasize instrument shapes or facial expressions.
donts: Do not use drop shadows, gradients, or outer glows on any text.
Do not use more than two different font families.
Do not center-align any text elements.
Do not use full-color photography; convert all imagery to high-contrast monochrome.
Do not clutter the design with decorative borders or excessive graphic flourishes.

critique_hoodie_back.summary: The design is a high-energy, visually dense graphic suitable for character-based streetwear. While the illustration quality is strong, the composition suffers from 'visual noise' where the background elements compete with the character, and the logo placement feels slightly disconnected from the main action.

composition.note: The layout is balanced, but the background 'equalizer' bars and floating vinyl records create significant clutter that distracts from the central character.

color_harmony.note: Excellent use of a high-contrast blue and white palette against black; the neon glow effects are consistent and vibrant.

legibility.note: The 'DJ RIOT' text is clear, though the logo icon above it is slightly redundant given the character is already wearing headphones.

focal_point.note: The eye is pulled between the character's face and the DJ deck hand; the competing visual weight makes it hard to settle on one point.

strengths: Effective use of glow effects to create depth

fixes.issue: Background clutter competing with the character
fixes.fix: Reduce the opacity or blur the background equalizer bars and floating vinyl records to push them further into the background depth.
Remove the large headphone logo icon above the 'DJ RIOT' text to allow the text to sit higher and breathe, or replace it with a more unique brand emblem.

fixes.issue: Lack of separation between hand and deck
fixes.fix: Add a subtle outer glow or rim light to the fingers touching the vinyl to ensure the hand doesn't blend into the dark record surface.
Apply a slight warp or perspective shift to the 'DJ RIOT' text so it feels like it is sitting on the same plane as the DJ deck rather than floating in front of the garment.

critique_hoodie_back.judgment_source: Scores and fixes are model judgments (Gemini vision) grounded in the uploaded image; format and dimensions in this response are read from the file header in code.
